response: The fundamental bottleneck in local AI inference and training has long been the memory capacity of the Graphics Processing Unit (GPU). In a conventional discrete GPU (dGPU) architecture, the processor and its memory are physically separate entities. The GPU contains its own high-bandwidth memory (HBM or GDDR), which is typically limited to 12GB, 24GB, or 48GB depending on the tier of the card.
